# Flood insurance

Started worrying after Storm Babet (Oct 2023) when Meanwood Beck came up over the footpath by the park and into the gardens on Green Road. We're about 140 m from it, 9 m higher up. Probably fine. "Probably" isn't a word I like.

## Our actual risk

- Environment Agency long-term map, checked 2 Mar 2024: **Flood Zone 1** for the property itself (less than 0.1% chance a year from watercourses). Surface water: "low" for the house, "medium" for the end of the street
- Postcode LS7 4QT. Insurers use their own maps (JBA, Ambiental), not the EA's, so this isn't the end of the question
- No previous flood claims on the property. Searches at purchase in 2014 came back clean

## Is it covered already?

Yes. Standard buildings and contents both include flood as a standard peril. Checked both policies:

- Buildings (Halifax, HBX-7716302): flood included, excess £1,000 for flood specifically. Ugh
- Contents (Direct Line): flood included, excess £250
- No separate policy needed in England unless you're in a high-risk zone and get refused

## Flood Re

The scheme that keeps cover affordable for high-risk properties built before 2009. Insurers pass the flood part of the premium to Flood Re at a fixed price set by council tax band. Band C: £168 buildings, £132 contents, for 2024/25.

Not relevant to us. Would matter for Lucy and Rob on Green Road, who were flooded in 2023 and saw their renewal jump from £340 to £1,890 before their broker moved them to a Flood Re backed insurer, now £560.

## The flat

Cardigan Road is on a slope, second floor. Zero flood exposure. Water risk there comes from above, see [[Landlord insurance]].

## Cheap things I did anyway

- Cleared gutters and the downpipe that backs up by the back door, see [[Gutter cleaning]]
- Bought 4 water-absorbent sacks (FloodSax, £39.99 for 5), in the garage
- Photos of every room for the contents inventory, in Google Photos album "Inventory-2024"
- Moved the box of paper files (tax records to 2018) up off the garage floor onto shelves
